messages:
alex: Quick proposal — tweak continuous-batcher to bias against forming large microbatches when KV hit rate < 0.65 and median_seq_len < 64. Add a per-shard token_budget target so we don’t oversubscribe GPU memory during KV miss storms.

maya: Can you sketch the heuristic? Is this just an extra threshold on batch growth?

alex: Yeah, idea: batch grows normally until either max_batch_tokens or max_clients reached. New rule: if kv_hit_rate(window=60s) < kv_low_watermark -> cap growth to min(max_batch_tokens, token_budget_target * (kv_hit_rate + 0.1)). That makes the batch smaller when misses spike.

sam: Interesting. My worry: smaller batches -> worse throughput, potential p95 regressions for common paths. Do we have profiling to show tradeoff?

igor: Ran a 3h canary on stage with this enabled (10% router split). Quick numbers:
- baseline: p50=85ms, p95=210ms, throughput=12.1k tok/s, cost index=1.00, kv_hit=0.62
- new heuristic: p50=90ms, p95=232ms, throughput=13.1k tok/s, cost index=0.88, kv_hit=0.71
Notes: overall token cost down ~12%, throughput up since fewer wasted retry/eviction cycles. Small p95 bump on some short-chat models.

alex: thanks igor. The p95 increase worries me but cost gains are decent. We should add a soft-429 fallback so that when queue length + token_budget_util > soft_limit we return a soft 429 with Retry-After rather than letting GPU queue explode.

maya: What do you mean by soft-429? Policy details?

alex: Soft-429 = a controlled rejection that preserves client-level semantics (429 with a Retry-After and header X-Backpressure-Reason). We’ll maintain a decaying token_leases counter per-customer. On soft-429 we decrement lease and increment a short-lived backoff ticket.

sam: Couple of implementation notes:
- we need instrumentation: token_budget_utilization, kv_hit_by_model_bucket, soft_429_rate per-route
- add an opt-in flag per-tenant (default off for enterprise with committed capacity)

igor: implementation snippet I used in canary (pseudo):
```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  token_budget_target: 4096
  kv_low_watermark: 0.65
  token_budget_window_secs: 60
  soft_429:
    enabled: true
    soft_limit: 0.9   # fraction of token_budget_target
    retry_after_secs: 2
```

maya: Also saw a perf-bot alert during the run (small regression on short-seq p99). @perf-bot can you paste the alert?

perf-bot: [alert] perf/regression/service=continuous-batcher model=chat-small seq_bucket=<32 tokens> metric=p99_latency change=+6.3% window=60m run_id=canary-17685

sam: That matches the p95 bump. Maybe we can make the heuristic-aware: if model.prefers_low_latency == true then relax kv_low_watermark for that model (allow larger batches even on lower kv_hit). Fallback: apply soft-429 earlier for those models so latency-sensitive apps fail-fast rather than queueing.

alex: Good idea. Add per-model override and an allowlist. Also add a roll-forward that slowly increases canary from 10 -> 30% if p95 stays within +7% and soft-429 rate < 1%.

igor: Action items from canary:
- telemetry: add "token_budget_utilization", "kv_hit_rate_by_model_bucket", "soft_429_rate" (done)
- config: expose token_budget_target and soft_limit per-shard (PR open: D1234)
- experiment: run 24h canary with per-model overrides for latency-sensitive routes

maya: I'll OWN the dashboards for the next canary. Will add alert if soft_429_rate > 0.5% or p95 delta > 7% for any important route.

sam: Dev note: be careful with kernel selection — smaller batch tokens may change kernel path (multihead -> singlehead) and that can cost us on certain sequence-length distributions. Add kernel-path histogram to perf telemetry.

alex: Good call. Also add a safety: if kernel-switching_count(window=60s) > 50% for a shard, temporarily disable the token_budget cap for 30s to avoid oscillation.

igor: TL;DR from canary: cost down, throughput up, small latency regression for very short sequences. Next step: opt-in per-model relax and soft-429 policy + 24h canary.

maya: LGTM. I'll schedule the 24h canary and post results here. :thumbsup:

sam: Also we should document the new config in ops playbook and add a command to toggle soft-429 for a shard: `./ctl shard set-config --shard $ID --continuous-batcher.soft_429.enabled=true`

alex: Thanks team. Let's keep defaults conservative and expose knobs. We'll iterate after 24h canary.

perf-bot: [info] experiment canary-17685 metrics posted to /dashboards/continuous-batcher/canary-17685

maya: Posted first 3h dashboard snapshot: /dashboards/continuous-batcher/canary-17685/snapshot-3h

alex: closing loop — folks, please comment if you want earlier rollback conditions. I'll open the rollout PR with docs + rollout plan.
